chapter: Complaints to Senator Eastland, FCC and WDSU
title: WDSU's reply that the script was not kept
summary: WDSU's operations manager says scripts are kept only a year, recalls nothing derogatory, and says he knows the ODJB started it all.

There's an answer there to this, WDSU. Alright, this is WDSU channel 6, I'm sorry, WDSU TV channel 6, New Orleans, WDSU Broadcasting Corporation, 520 Royal Street, New Orleans 16, Louisiana, Tulane 4371. January 4th, 1957, Mr. Nick LaRocca, 2218 Cousin Street, New Orleans 13, Louisiana. Dear Nick, our manager, Mr. Robert Swayze has passed to me your letter of January 13th relative to a program on jazz music which we carried in the summer of 1935. I have made a rather thorough search for the script of this program to which you refer. But unfortunately, our continuity department keeps a script for television programs for a period of one year as is required by station policy and commission rules. The program to which you refer was conducted by Almond Hug and was announced by Bob Nelson of our staff. Bob recalls very little of the running conversation in which his chief duty was the questioning of Almond regarding the history of jazz music. Any statements were made by Almond Hug and I feel certain he would probably be able to enlighten you. I have a fairly vivid recollection of the program but do not recall any derogatory statements regarding yourself. Since I am one of the uncounted brilliance of persons who know that you and the original Dixieland jazz band started the whole thing, I feel certain that I would recall any unfavorable comment in this regard. We are retaining the 12 Fortestad copies in our file and should you care to have them returned, we would be very happy to do so. I am indeed sorry that we were unable to supply you with this trip requested. Kindest personal regards. Sincerely yours, Stanley Holloway. I'm sorry, Stanley Holliday. Stanley Holliday, Manager of Operations, initials SHDC. Let me close with Almond Hug with regards to what has been said.
